narrative: Markets are trading a sharp hawkish repricing following hotter-than-expected October US CPI (0.4% m/m headline, 0.3% core), which sparked Fed rate-hike bets and aggressive Treasury yield surges. Federal Reserve officials struck a decidedly hawkish tone, with Lorie Logan calling for at least two more hikes, Christopher Waller urging the reversal of insurance cuts, and Austan Goolsbee labeling inflation prints as borderline disturbing. The surge in real yields, combined with regulatory scrutiny and chip export tensions, has driven a steep $1.7 trillion drawdown in Nvidia. Concurrently, broader equities are under pressure from tightening financial conditions and high AI debt financing costs. Meanwhile, crude oil tumbled 24% in November amid growth headwinds and geopolitical de-escalation, while gold slipped on rising yields.

Nasdaq.why: Pressured by surging Treasury yields, high debt financing costs, and a sharp drawdown in Nvidia per anchors and Tim Urbanowicz, though Yvonne Man notes futures resilience backed by long-term AI demand.

S&P 500.why: Faces downside risks from aggressive Fed policy tightening, sticky inflation, and elevated valuation risks warned by Diane Swonk.

Gold.why: Spot prices slipped toward $4,035/oz as rate-sensitive precious metals retreat under pressure from rising real yields and a strengthening USD.

Oil.why: Brent crude tumbled 24% in November due to macroeconomic growth headwinds noted by Chris Phelan, alongside geopolitical de-escalation pricing.
